text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Basque separatist group ETA claims third victim in two days.
- Catalan leader Jordi Pujol demands modification of digital television decree in Congress.
EL MUNDO
- Transport strike prompts close of factories and shortages.
DIARIO 16
- ETA shoots dead Patxi Arratibel in Tolosa streets as he takes part in carnival parade.
ABC
- Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar meets Catalan leader Jordi Pujol in climate of serenity and absence of tension that has marked Spanish life after three ETA attacks in two days.
CINCO DIAS
- Independent transporters go too far with strike which leads to shortages in middle of Spain.
- Pujol disagrees with Aznar on digital TV decree and without CiU support government cannot pass 1998 budget.
- Bank of Spain governor Luis Angel Rojo insinuates that next interest rate cut on hold in January economic report.
- Telefonica privatisation will bring Treasury 150 billion pesetas more than forecast in budget.
EXPANSION
- Bank of Spain confirms greater dynamism in economy.
- Campofrio, Omsa and Navidul declare "ham war" on Andalucia local government.
- Savings banks attract 405 billion pesetas in January, the highest monthly increase in history.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Bank of Spain says economic growth 2.2 percent in 1996.
- Bank of Spain suggests in Economic Bulletin that there is still room for further mergers in Spanish financial market.
- Government will try to place 25 percent of electricity group Endesa in market in October.
